To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the 5-year impact factor is more field-normalized than the 2-year impact factor, (b) fractional counting of citations reduces the between-field variation in the impact factors more than it reduces the between-field variance in total citation counts, (c) percentile ranking of impact factors is a powerful normalization tool across all fields, and (d) the combination of fractional counting and percentile ranking of impact factor values is a powerful tool for field normalization.

(1) fractional counting reduces the between-field variance in IF5 by a factor of 10, (2) percentile ranks of IFs reduce the variance further by a factor of two, and (3) the combined effect of fractional counting and transformation into percentile ranks reduces the between-field effect by a factor of five, and thus provides a field-normalized measure of journal impact.

the normalization of impact factors across broad fields of science requires fractional counting and percentile ranks.
